channel.title: AffiLayer Blog
channel.description: Launch notes and plain notes on affiliate marketing — what we built, what changed, and what we learned running the network.

item.title: How We Review Conversions Before They Become Payable
item.description: Every conversion on AffiLayer is recorded as pending and reviewed by hand before it becomes payable. Here is what the review checks, and what happens next.

item.title: Pending, Approved, Rejected, Reversed: Reading Your Ledger
item.description: Every commission on AffiLayer sits in one of four ledger states — pending, approved, rejected or reversed. Here is what each one means, and when it pays.

item.title: Dating and Sweepstakes CPA: Traffic That Converts
item.description: Dating and sweepstakes traffic is fast, mobile and impulse-led — and the verticals where a misleading creative costs you the account fastest. What to watch.

item.title: Gaming CPA Offers: Traffic, Payouts and Player Quality
item.description: Gaming traffic is fast, huge and mixed in quality. Installs pay for volume, deposits pay for players — and that difference decides if the traffic is worth it.

item.title: Finance CPA Offers: What Converts and What to Watch
item.description: Finance CPA pays for intent — but compliance and lead quality decide whether a lead is worth anything. What converts, what gets rejected, and what to watch.

item.title: Setting Caps and Payouts Without Losing Money
item.description: Daily caps, total caps and the payout model are your budget controls. How to set them, what happens when a cap is hit, and when the money actually moves.

item.title: Approving Affiliates: What to Check Before You Say Yes
item.description: Approval is a gate, not a guarantee. Check traffic source, vertical fit, GEO and quality signals — and know what saying yes does and does not promise.

item.title: What Advertisers Should Put in an Offer Brief
item.description: An offer brief is the agreement before the agreement: payout, caps, countries, traffic rules, conversion definition. What to write, and why each line matters.

item.title: How to publish your first offer on AffiLayer: payouts, caps, geos and traffic rules
item.description: Publish an offer in four parts: the payout and conversion action, the caps, the countries and devices, and the traffic rules. Then approve affiliates.

item.title: Affiliate fraud: the patterns that get accounts rejected — and how to stay clean
item.description: Bots, misleading creatives, forced clicks and incentivised traffic. The patterns are old, the detection is straightforward, and clean traffic has nothing to fear.

item.title: Geo targeting in CPA: why the same offer pays differently in every country
item.description: The same offer in the United States and in Brazil is two different offers: different audiences, different payouts, different rules. Geo decides.

item.title: Offer caps explained: daily caps, total caps, and what happens when a cap is hit
item.description: A cap is the advertiser saying "this much, and no more". Daily caps reset; total caps end the offer. A capped click is refused, not wasted.

item.title: What does Net30 mean? Payout timing, holds and the real wait for your first payment
item.description: Net30 means approved commissions become payable 30 days after the end of the month in which they were approved. A worked example, with dates.

item.title: Sub IDs explained: the 5 parameters that tell you which click earned
item.description: Sub IDs are labels you attach to your own clicks — campaign, placement, creative. Five of them, and they are how you learn what actually converts.

item.title: How to choose a CPA network: 7 checks before you send your first click
item.description: Seven checks before you send traffic: tracking you can audit, a ledger you can read, honest payout terms, and no promises the network cannot keep.

item.title: Why your conversions go missing: pixels, ad blockers and the case for server-to-server
item.description: A conversion that never reaches the network never pays. Pixels lose conversions to browsers; server-to-server reporting does not depend on them.

item.title: How affiliate tracking actually works: click IDs, postbacks and S2S
item.description: A click gets a unique ID, the conversion is linked back to it, and the record is signed and deduplicated. That chain is the whole of tracking.

item.title: What is a SmartLink? One link, many offers — and what ours does differently
item.description: A SmartLink is one tracking link that routes each visitor to an eligible offer for their country and device. Ours uses fixed, published rules.

item.title: CPA vs CPL vs CPS vs CPC: which payout model pays you, and when
item.description: CPA, CPL, CPS and CPC differ in one thing: what triggers payment. The trigger decides who bears the risk — and when a commission becomes payable.

item.title: What is a CPA network? How affiliates, advertisers and the network fit together
item.description: A CPA network connects advertisers who pay for a defined action with affiliates who drive it — and handles tracking, attribution and payouts.
